mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative correlation between GDPC1 YoY change and returns is not statistically significant at p < 0.01.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces wage growth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline (p > 0.05), or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and drags down the S&P 500 over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered episodes (p > 0.10), or the trigger is not followed by a decline in sector-specific indices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weak inflation, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for 2 months
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the joint signal does not outperform the single-proxy FEDFUNDS signal in predictive accuracy.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12M MA and RSAFS > 12M MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes (p > 0.05), or the joint signal fails to improve predictive power over the single best proxy.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which precedes tighter monetary policy and profit margin compression, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods (p > 0.10), or the trigger is not followed by a tightening in monetary policy proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a construction sector recovery, which boosts materials and financial sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes (p > 0.05), or the housing recovery is not accompanied by broader industrial recovery.
